id: title:Gilbert09:stop retrying a postgres sync whose cursor no longer matches a boolean column

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a non-retryable error classification and regression test for PostgreSQL boolean parsing failures in warehouse incremental syncs, preventing infinite retry loops when source column types change.
review.reason: Score 2 assigned: The change adds a substantive, bounded capability. P1.F1.H1 introduces a specific, non-retryable error entry for PostgreSQL boolean parsing failures, distinguishing this failure mode from retryable ones to prevent infinite loops. P1.F2.H1 adds corresponding test assertions, providing regression coverage. This demonstrates a correctness and reliability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The tier relies on the assumption that distinguishing this specific database error and its classification as non-retryable is a substantive improvement rather than a narrow maintenance fix; no broader systemic changes or wider adoption metrics are visible.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new non-retryable error entry for PostgreSQL boolean type parsing failures in incremental warehouse syncs.
observations.code_quote: "invalid input syntax for type boolean": "PostHog tried to resume this table's incremental sync from a cursor value that your database can no longer parse as a boolean. This usually means the incremental field's column type changed at the source after this sync started. Please reset and fully re-sync this table, or pick a different incremental field.",
observations.posthog_connection: Allows PostHog warehouse ingestion to distinguish and stop retrying when a source column's declared type changes from the configured incremental field type, preventing infinite retry loops on unparseable boolean cursors.

observations.behavior: Adds test assertions for boolean-specific parsing errors alongside existing integer/bigint error checks.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression coverage for the boolean type-change detection and non-retryable classification.
